_comment: Tier 3 watch list. Each entry aggregates iNaturalist observations into a
phase estimate for one phenomenon at one place.
precision is deliberately 'regional' for every entry: a cluster of citizen
observations locates a phenomenon to a landscape, never to a point. Morel
hunters in particular obscure their locations on purpose, so treating that
signal as point-precise would be both wrong and rude.

watches.name: Morel Emergence (Great Lakes)
watches.blurb: Morel season tracked through forager reports. Locations are deliberately vague — hunters guard their patches.

watches.name: Monarch Overwintering Roosts
watches.blurb: Hundreds of millions of monarchs clustering on oyamel fir, dense enough to bend the branches.

watches.name: Christmas Island Red Crab Migration
watches.blurb: Around 50 million crabs cross the island to spawn, triggered by the first heavy rains and timed to a specific lunar phase.

watches.name: Synchronous Firefly Display
watches.blurb: One of few firefly species that flashes in unison. Viewing access is lottery-allocated by the National Park Service.

watches.name: Horseshoe Crab Spawning
watches.blurb: Spawning peaks on new and full moon high tides, drawing the red knot migration that feeds on the eggs.

watches.name: Green Turtle Nesting
watches.blurb: The largest green turtle rookery in the western hemisphere. Night beach access requires a licensed guide.

watches.name: Sockeye Salmon Run
watches.blurb: Spawning sockeye turn the river red. Dominant-year runs are an order of magnitude larger than off years.

watches.name: Humpback Bubble-Net Feeding
watches.blurb: Cooperative bubble-net feeding, a learned behaviour passed between individuals rather than inherited.
